title: casting rides a door
what: A ticket enters the corpus through a door that refuses a malformed one, instead of by a hand writing a JSON file that nothing checks.
why: The ticket corpus is what every voyage anchors to — a proof's claim, a crossing's gate, a chart's clain all resolve against a ticket file. And a ticket enters that corpus because I typed a JSON file correctly. Nothing refuses a missing field, a duplicate id, an unparseable workflow string, or a berth path that resolves to nothing. The lived symptom is already measured on the corpus it produced: 263 tickets, `author` on 6%, `owner` in ~42 different phrasings, `cast_by` holding two different meanings. That is what an ungated store looks like from the inside, and every voyage is leaning on it.
how: The IOU is stated at cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py:38 and has been standing there: '/sorted files a ticket by writing a file; nothing refuses the write.' MEASURED 2026-09-09, and stated at the width the instrument actually covers: no Python module in cairn/, skills/ or bin/ creates a ticket file. The creator is a HAND — CC's, following /sorted step 5 — 264 times. cairn/tools/base/transitions.py has a ticket write door (set_phase, built under 9e7867aa1056) but it writes the PHASE on an existing ticket and explicitly refuses a `ticket=` the world does not hold, so creation is out of its scope by design. Approach: (1) a `cast_ticket` door beside set_phase in the same module, taking the /sorted berth path and writing the ticket file from it — the berth already holds the judged packet, so the door composes an existing judged artifact rather than re-judging; (2) it refuses on the store charter's required fields, on a duplicate id, on a workflow string parse_workflow cannot read, and on an intent_berth or sorted_berth that does not resolve; (3) it journals the act, so 'who cast this and when' becomes a record rather than an inference; (4) /sorted step 5 stops saying 'write the file' and starts saying 'fire the door'. DO NOT retro-red the 264 existing tickets — watchme_spec.py:34 records that exact stone being paid for twice already ('A CHECK THAT RETRO-REDS EVERY OPEN BOAT IS A CHECK THAT GETS DISABLED'), so the door gates ENTRY and a separate sweep reports the backlog without failing anything.
traces_to: Law 4 — the rule that a ticket must be well-formed is real, is written down in the store charter, and is enforced by nothing but my care while typing; that is the definition of a tracked debt rather than a resting state. Law 6 — the tickets store has an owner and an owner gates writes, and today writes arrive ambiently. Law 8 — the corpus is what every voyage's proof is anchored to, and an unvalidated corpus is a peer being leaned on without ever having been proven.
falsifier: DONE when a ticket cannot enter CairnCommons/tickets/ except through the door; when a malformed cast is refused with every lack named in one pass; when the act is journaled; and when /sorted step 5 fires the door rather than describing a file write. HORIZON: the next 10 casts after PROVED — all 10 journaled, zero hand-written files. WRONG INTENT if the door lands and hand-written tickets continue beside it, which is the measured failure shape of the phase door it sits next to (built 2026-09-08, 13 records in four days, then no caller); a door with no callers is worse than no door, because it reads as physics from the outside while the writes go round it.
children: none, because the judge, the writer and the journal are one door over one store — and _write_ticket already exists at transitions.py:2163, so the byte-level write is composed rather than built. The backlog SWEEP is not a child either: it reports and never fails, so it cannot hold this ticket open.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the-casting-door-has-callers) -> PROVED

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: tickets journaled through the door, tickets arriving unjournaled, and the distinct calendar days spanned
watchme.consumer: whoever casts the next ticket, and e71983e8d76c (author + via), which cannot be enforced at all until this door exists
watchme.enough: 10 consecutive casts journaled through the door with zero unjournaled arrivals, across at least 3 distinct calendar days. THE DAYS CLAUSE IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS COPIED FROM THE FAILURE NEXT DOOR: the phase door took 13 records in FOUR DAYS and then went silent forever, so a burst on one day is exactly the shape that must not clear this watch. It can also go back down — one unjournaled arrival re-opens it.
watchme.trigger: each ticket appearing in CairnCommons/tickets/ — the store's own growth is the trigger, so a hand-written file fires the watch by existing

gates_bound.check_type: proofs beside the code, run twice, sealed under the tester with isolation
a red at PROVEME kicks back to this ticket
a sweep counts tickets whose creation is not journaled; new entries after PROVED must be zero
gates_bound.gate: the door is the only path
gates_bound.why: the whole ticket is this sentence. A door beside a still-open side path is decoration, and the store next door proved the pattern (55dc1f3d799b) by making the door the ONLY path rather than the preferred one

in: cairn/tools/base/transitions.py — the new casting door, beside set_phase; _write_ticket at line 2163 is the byte-level writer and is composed, not rebuilt
skills/sorted/SKILL.md step 5 + skills/sorted/intention+why.json — 'file to CairnCommons' becomes 'fire the door'
CairnCommons/tickets/_charter+why.json — the required-field set the door judges against
a backlog SWEEP that reports the 264 existing tickets and fails nothing
out: RETRO-REDDING THE 264. Hard bound, not a preference: watchme_spec.py:34 records this stone being paid for twice, most recently 2026-08-03 when a scrub retagged 50 cast tickets and the rule redded all 50. Its conclusion is in the file — 'A CHECK THAT RETRO-REDS EVERY OPEN BOAT IS A CHECK THAT GETS DISABLED.'
Extending set_phase to also create. Its refusal of a ticket the world does not hold is load-bearing — it stops a typo'd id from silently minting a ticket.
A git pre-commit hook on tickets/. Fires after the reasoning is gone, and cannot journal who cast it (one committer on the commons repo).
Reshaping `owner` or migrating authorship — that is e71983e8d76c, this ticket's child in effect, and it needs this door to be enforceable at all.

open_for_akien: One, and it is a spec choice so it waits for you rather than for evidence: should the casting door live in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py beside set_phase, or in a tickets-store module of its own? Beside set_phase is where the byte writer and the journaling already are, and it is what I have assumed. Against it: transitions.py is already the biggest file in the system and it is the WORKFLOW authority, while this is a STORE door — the two are different jobs sharing an address. My read is beside set_phase for this build, with the split as its own later question once both doors have callers, because splitting an unused door is rearranging.
